class.name: NNResponseCurve
class.brief_description: A parametric curve that maps a [code]0..1[/code] input to a [code]0..1[/code] output.
class.description: Assign to any [code]activation_curve[/code] property, such as [member NNConsideration.activation_curve] or [member NNNQSSearchCriteria.activation_curve], instead of drawing a [Curve]. [method sample] clamps the input to [code]0..1[/code], applies [member curve_type] using [member slope] and [member exponent], shifts the result by [member y_shift], clamps it to [code]0..1[/code], and finally inverts it when [member invert] is [code]true[/code]. With the default parameters each type gives its canonical [code]0..1[/code] shape: [constant CURVE_LINEAR] is [code]x[/code], [constant CURVE_POLYNOMIAL] is [code]x^2[/code], [constant CURVE_LOGISTIC] is an S centred at [code]0.5[/code], [constant CURVE_NORMAL] a bell peaking at [code]0.5[/code], [constant CURVE_SINE] a hump that rises from [code]0[/code] through [code]1[/code] at [code]0.5[/code] back to [code]0[/code], and [constant CURVE_STEP] a threshold at [code]0.5[/code]. [member x_shift] moves the curve horizontally, so the centre of the symmetric shapes sits at [code]0.5 + x_shift[/code]. [member slope] scales the output and [member exponent] controls how sharply each shape bends; see each [enum CurveType] constant for its formula, where [code]u = x - x_shift[/code]. [member preview] is a [Curve] baked from these parameters for the inspector only; evaluation never samples it.

method.name: sample
method.description: Returns the curve's value at [param x]. The input is clamped to [code]0..1[/code], a non-finite result becomes [code]0.0[/code], and the result is clamped to [code]0..1[/code] and then inverted when [member invert] is [code]true[/code].

members.member: The shape sampled by [method sample]. See each [enum CurveType] constant for its formula. [constant CURVE_LINEAR] and [constant CURVE_STEP] ignore [member exponent].

Steepness of the [constant CURVE_POLYNOMIAL], [constant CURVE_EXPONENTIAL], [constant CURVE_LOGISTIC], [constant CURVE_LOGIT], [constant CURVE_NORMAL] and [constant CURVE_SINE] shapes. Larger values sharpen the curve, except [constant CURVE_LOGIT], which flattens as its inverse logistic sharpens; the default [code]2.0[/code] gives each type its canonical shape. Ignored when [member curve_type] is [constant CURVE_LINEAR] or [constant CURVE_STEP], where it is also hidden in the inspector.
If [code]true[/code], the clamped result is flipped: [code]y[/code] becomes [code]1 - y[/code].
A read-only, non-saved [Curve] with 65 evenly spaced points baked from the current parameters so the inspector can draw the shape. It is regenerated after a parameter changes.
Multiplier applied before [member y_shift]. With the default [code]1.0[/code] each type covers the full [code]0..1[/code] output range.

Horizontal offset subtracted from the clamped input before the curve is evaluated. Positive values move the curve to the right; the centre of [constant CURVE_LOGISTIC], [constant CURVE_LOGIT], [constant CURVE_NORMAL] and [constant CURVE_SINE], and the threshold of [constant CURVE_STEP], sit at [code]0.5 + x_shift[/code].
Vertical offset added after the curve is evaluated and before the result is clamped to [code]0..1[/code] and inverted.

constants.constant: An exponential ramp: [code]slope * (exp(exponent * u) - 1) / (exp(exponent) - 1)[/code], falling back to [code]slope * u[/code] when [member exponent] is nearly [code]0[/code]. Rises slowly and then steeply from [code]0[/code] at [code]u = 0[/code] to [code]slope[/code] at [code]u = 1[/code].
A straight line from [code]0[/code] at [code]u = 0[/code] to [code]slope[/code] at [code]u = 1[/code]: [code]slope * u[/code]. Ignores [member exponent].
An S-curve crossing [code]slope * 0.5[/code] at [code]u = 0.5[/code]: [code]slope / (1 + exp(-5 * exponent * (u - 0.5)))[/code]. Steeper as [member exponent] grows.

The inverse of the logistic curve: [code]slope * (0.5 + ln(u / (1 - u)) / (5 * exponent))[/code], with [code]u[/code] clamped to [code]0.0001..0.9999[/code]. Crosses [code]slope * 0.5[/code] at [code]u = 0.5[/code]; a larger [member exponent] flattens its middle, mirroring the steeper logistic curve.
A bell curve peaking at [code]slope[/code] when [code]u = 0.5[/code]: [code]slope * exp(-10 * exponent * (u - 0.5)^2)[/code]. Narrower as [member exponent] grows.

A power curve from [code]0[/code] at [code]u = 0[/code] to [code]slope[/code] at [code]u = 1[/code]: [code]slope * u ^ exponent[/code]. With the default [member exponent] of [code]2.0[/code] it is a parabola that rises slowly and then steeply.

A smooth hump: [code]slope * 0.5 * (1 - cos(PI * exponent * u))[/code]. With the default [member exponent] of [code]2.0[/code] it rises from [code]0[/code] through [code]slope[/code] at [code]u = 0.5[/code] back to [code]0[/code]; with [code]1.0[/code] it is a smooth ease from [code]0[/code] to [code]slope[/code].
A threshold: [code]slope[/code] when [code]u >= 0.5[/code] and [code]0[/code] otherwise. Ignores [member exponent].
